headline: Farage quits his seat and asks voters to decide

sources.title: Reform UK's Nigel Farage says he'll quit as a lawmaker and seek re-election to clear name
Why has UK Reform's Nigel Farage resigned as MP? What happens next?
Reform UK's Farage resigns as MP amid funding scandal, forcing by-election
Nigel Farage resigns as MP so why is he triggering a by-election? | BBC News (video, BBC Politics)

chunks.text: Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform UK, said he would {{step down}} from his seat in Parliament. He explained that he would {{hand in}} his [[resignation]] as a [[lawmaker]] and then {{run for}} the same seat again in a [[by-election]]. Farage represents the [[constituency]] of Clacton in eastern England, which he won in 2024. He said he wanted local voters to decide his future.

verbs.wrong: To take a break from work for some time
verbs.correct: To leave an important job or position

verbs.wrong: To announce something to the public
verbs.correct: To give a document to someone in charge

verbs.wrong: To ask people to vote in an election
verbs.correct: To compete in an election for a position

chunks.text: Farage's [[announcement]] comes as a parliamentary [[watchdog]] has started to {{look into}} money he received. The Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards is [[examining]] [[donations]] that Farage did not report, including a reported 5 million pound gift from a cryptocurrency businessman based in Thailand. Reporters {{pointed out}} that British rules [[require]] members of Parliament to [[declare]] large gifts. The [[investigation]] could decide whether Farage broke Parliament's standards on money.

verbs.wrong: To ask someone questions in a public meeting
verbs.correct: To examine or investigate something carefully

verbs.wrong: To criticize someone in the news
verbs.correct: To tell someone about a fact

chunks.text: Farage said he had done nothing wrong. He told reporters, 'I have not [[broken the law]] in any way at all.' Farage did not {{own up to}} any [[wrongdoing]], and he [[made clear]] he would not {{back down}}. He decided to {{speak out}} against the process. Farage described the vote as a fight of 'people vs the [[establishment]]' and said local people should judge his actions.

verbs.wrong: To be as good as people expected
verbs.correct: To admit that you did something wrong

verbs.wrong: To stay silent about a problem
verbs.correct: To stop demanding something or give in

verbs.wrong: To defend yourself in a court
verbs.correct: To say publicly what you think

chunks.text: Because Farage chose to {{stand down}}, a by-election will now [[take place]] in Clacton. The Labour, Conservative, and Liberal Democrat parties {{ruled out}} putting up their own candidates for the vote. Reform UK offered to pay for the election and said it would {{carry on}} its [[campaign]]. Farage, who won Clacton in 2024, [[is expected to]] {{take on}} few strong [[rivals]] and win the seat back.

tf.s: Nigel Farage decided to step down from his seat in Parliament.
tf.why: Farage stepped down (left his position), which is exactly what he announced.

tf.s: Farage said he would carry on in his seat instead of leaving Parliament.
tf.why: Farage stepped down (left his seat). Carry on means to continue, the opposite of what he did.

tf.s: Reform UK ruled out paying for the by-election.
tf.why: Reform UK offered to pay for the by-election. Rule out means to decide against something, which is untrue here.

tf.s: Farage owned up to wrongdoing over the donations.
tf.why: Farage did not own up to (admit) any wrongdoing. He said he had done nothing wrong.

tf.s: A parliamentary watchdog began to look into the donations Farage received.
tf.why: The watchdog looked into (started to investigate) the donations, which is happening.

tf.s: Farage said he would run for his old seat again in the by-election.
tf.why: Farage will run for (compete for) his seat again, which he announced.
